bridgeDevice.note: the first board to enumerate gets ttyACM0; with several MCU boards, pin each by its USB serial number (a udev rule or /dev/serial/by-id) rather than by order

source.where: Change the primary UART: on 'Raspberry Pi Zero W, Zero 2 W, 3, and 4' the PL011 UART0 'is connected to the Bluetooth controller by default, so the mini UART is the primary UART on GPIO 14 and 15'; table 'Linux device nodes for UARTs': /dev/ttyAMA0 = first PL011 (UART0), /dev/ttyS0 = mini UART

alternatives.note: on Raspberry Pi 4 GPIO14/15 default to the mini UART (/dev/ttyS0), whose baud rate follows the VPU core clock ('Mini UART and core frequency'), and the primary UART carries the Linux serial console by default. For a reliable link to the MCU board, give UART0 to GPIO14/15 (disable Bluetooth with the disable-bt overlay, or move it with miniuart-bt) and turn the serial console off
alternatives.via: UART0 on header pins 8 (GPIO14 TX) and 10 (GPIO15 RX)
